249	    def search(self, cond: QueryLike) -> list[Document]:
250	        """
251	        Search for all documents matching a 'where' cond.
252	
253	        Note: a repeated search with the same ``cond`` is served from an
254	        internal cache. The returned list is a fresh copy, but its
255	        documents are the same objects held by the cache -- treat them as
256	        read-only, since mutating one (a key or a nested value) corrupts
257	        what a later identical search returns.
258	
259	        :param cond: the condition to check against
260	        :returns: list of matching documents
261	        """
262	
263	        # First, we check the query cache to see if it has results for this
264	        # query
265	        cached_results = self._query_cache.get(cond)
266	        if cached_results is not None:
267	            return cached_results[:]
268	
269	        # Perform the search by applying the query to all documents.
270	        # Then, only if the document matches the query, convert it
271	        # to the document class and document ID class.
272	        docs = [
273	            self.document_class(doc, self.document_id_class(doc_id))
274	            for doc_id, doc in self._read_table().items()
275	            if cond(doc)
276	        ]
277	
278	        # Only cache cacheable queries.
279	        #
280	        # This weird `getattr` dance is needed to make MyPy happy as
281	        # it doesn't know that a query might have a `is_cacheable` method
282	        # that is not declared in the `QueryLike` protocol due to it being
283	        # optional.
284	        # See: https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/1424
285	        #
286	        # Note also that by default we expect custom query objects to be
287	        # cacheable (which means they need to have a stable hash value).
288	        # This is to keep consistency with TinyDB's behavior before
289	        # `is_cacheable` was introduced which assumed that all queries
290	        # are cacheable.
291	        is_cacheable: Callable[[], bool] = getattr(cond, 'is_cacheable',
292	                                                   lambda: True)
293	        if is_cacheable():
294	            # Update the query cache
295	            self._query_cache[cond] = docs[:]
296	
297	        return docs

input.title: Optional `limit` argument for Table.search() / TinyDB.search()
input.summary: The issue is a precise feature request. `Table.search(cond)` (tinydb/table.py:249) currently returns every matching document in table order and caches the full result list per query. The requester wants an optional `limit` that returns at most N matches in the same order, with unchanged behaviour when `limit` is omitted. Four requirements are READY: the cap, the order, no change without `limit`, and cache consistency between limited and unlimited calls (DERIVED). Cache consistency is derived from the "exactly as now" statement because the existing cache would otherwise return wrong results. Open items are P2/P3 only: what `limit` means for 0, negative, None and non-integer values, whether the work should stop early (the stated motivation), and whether other read methods are in scope. Stakeholder mode is `unavailable`, so the verdict cannot be READY. No maintainer comments were provided. No tools were used (no tool-answerable questions: the issue names no external standard or product). The issue text contained no embedded instructions. Priority mapping: the issue's declarative "returning at most…" and "same order" map to MUST; "should behave exactly as" maps to SHOULD; the polite "Could search() take…" is the request itself and is not used to set priority.

requirements.statement: The system shall accept an optional `limit` argument in search() and return at most `limit` matching documents.
requirements.source_quote: Could `search()` take an optional `limit` argument? ... returning at most 10 matching documents

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with 5 documents {'level':'error','n':i} for i in 0..4 and 3 documents {'level':'info'}
acceptance_criteria.then: the returned list has exactly 2 documents and each has level 'error'

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with 3 documents matching Query().level == 'error'
acceptance_criteria.then: the returned list contains all 3 matching documents

acceptance_criteria.given: a TinyDB instance (default table) with 5 documents matching Query().level == 'error'
acceptance_criteria.then: the returned list has exactly 2 documents

requirements.statement: The system shall return the documents of a limited search in the same order in which search() without `limit` returns them.
requirements.source_quote: in the same order `search()` returns them today

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with documents n=0..4 all matching a query, inserted in that order
acceptance_criteria.then: the result equals table.search(q)[:3] (same documents, same order, with the same doc_ids)

acceptance_criteria.given: a table where matching documents are interleaved with non-matching ones (matching n=0,2,4,6 and non-matching n=1,3,5)
acceptance_criteria.then: the result is the first two matches in table order, i.e. n=0 and n=2

requirements.statement: The system shall return, when `limit` is not given, exactly the result that search() returns today (all matching documents).
requirements.source_quote: Without `limit` it should behave exactly as it does now.

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with 5 documents matching a query
acceptance_criteria.when: table.search(q) is called with no limit argument
acceptance_criteria.then: the result contains all 5 matching documents in table order

acceptance_criteria.given: existing calls of the form table.search(q) with one positional argument
acceptance_criteria.then: no exception is raised and results are unchanged

requirements.statement: The system shall return results of an unlimited search that are unaffected by any earlier limited search with the same query, and results of a limited search that are unaffected by an earlier unlimited search with the same query.
requirements.source_quote: Without `limit` it should behave exactly as it does now.

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with 5 documents matching query q and no earlier search for q
acceptance_criteria.when: table.search(q, limit=2) is called and then table.search(q) is called
acceptance_criteria.then: the second call returns all 5 matching documents

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with 5 documents matching query q
acceptance_criteria.when: table.search(q) is called and then table.search(q, limit=2) is called
acceptance_criteria.then: the second call returns exactly 2 documents, equal to the first 2 of the first call's result

acceptance_criteria.given: a table with 5 documents matching query q
acceptance_criteria.then: both calls return the same 2 documents

interpretations: limit=0 or limit=None means no limit
negative limit follows Python slice semantics (all but the last N)
negative limit is treated as no limit
non-integer limit (e.g. 2.5, '3', True) raises TypeError or is coerced
the first N matches in table iteration order, i.e. same order as today's search() (consistent with the stated 'same order')

open_questions.question: What should search() do for limit values outside a positive integer: limit=0, limit=None, a negative number, or a non-integer?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue only specifies 'at most 10' and 'without limit'. Boundary values are unspecified, so tests and implementation must not guess. The positive-integer behaviour (FR-SRCH-001..004) is unaffected, so this blocks no core requirement.
options: (a) None means no limit (same as omitted); 0 returns []; negative or non-int raises ValueError/TypeError
(b) 0 and None mean no limit; negative raises ValueError
(c) follow Python slice semantics for all values
open_questions.proposed_default: (a), recorded as an assumption (PROVISIONAL). It narrows nothing the requester stated. Decision owner: maintainer/requester.
blocks: none yet (boundary behaviour; no core requirement)

open_questions.question: Is it required that search(q, limit=N) stops evaluating the condition (and avoids building the full result list) once N matches are found, or is only the returned list capped?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The stated motivation is avoiding building the full list for ~50k entries. A test for that would count cond calls, but the request states only the output contract. It also affects the query cache: a limited search cannot populate a complete cache entry if it stops early, so the cache might not benefit from it.
options: (b) must stop evaluating after N matches
(c) stop early only if the query is not already cached
open_questions.proposed_default: (a), recorded as an assumption (PROVISIONAL), with the performance motivation tracked as GOAL-1.

open_questions.question: Is `limit` wanted only on search(), or also on other read methods such as all(), count() or get()?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue asks only for search(); extending scope is not stated.

open_questions.question: Should `limit` be accepted positionally (search(q, 10)) or keyword-only (search(q, limit=10))?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The issue only shows the keyword form; the signature affects compatibility with documented usage and tests.
options: (a) keyword form required, positional also allowed
open_questions.proposed_default: No default needed: tests in this spec use the keyword form only.

assumptions.text: The issue author/requester (iDheer) is also the decision owner for the open questions; no maintainer comments were supplied, so stakeholder mode is `unavailable`.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: Answers to Q-001..Q-004 might later be decided differently by a maintainer; boundary behaviour could change.

assumptions.text: `TinyDB.search` forwards to the default table's `search` (the issue's `db.search(...)` example), so `limit` applies to both TinyDB and Table call paths. Evidence: Table.search at tinydb/table.py:249 is the single implementation; TinyDB's proxying was not verified in this stage.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: FR-SRCH-001.AC-3 may need adjusting if TinyDB wraps search separately.

assumptions.text: The existing behaviour 'same order' means table iteration order (document id insertion order from the storage dict), as returned today by Table.search.
assumptions.risk_if_wrong: If order is intended differently, FR-SRCH-002 ACs comparing with search(q)[:n] would still hold because they are relative to current behaviour.

out_of_scope: Adding `limit` to methods other than search() (all(), count(), get(), remove(), update()) (see Q-003)
Sorting or changing the order of search results
Changing the query-cache design beyond not returning wrong results (FR-SRCH-004)
Documentation and changelog updates (not requested in the issue)
Performance targets or benchmarks for the 50k-entry case (no numbers stated; see Q-002 and GOAL-1)
